title: Change One Letter at a Time

concept.title: Find the neighbours of a word through patterns with one wildcard letter
body: A *word ladder* turns the word `begin` into the word `end` by changing **one letter at a time**, where every word on the way must be in the dictionary. What is the smallest number of words in such a ladder (counting `begin` and `end`)? Words are nodes, and two words are neighbours when they differ in exactly one letter. A breadth-first search finds the shortest ladder.

The difficulty is to **find the neighbours quickly**. Comparing a word with all `k` words of the dictionary costs O(k * length) per word, O(k^2) in total: too slow for 5000 words. A better way: every word has `length` *patterns*, made by replacing one letter with `*`: `hot` has `*ot`, `h*t` and `ho*`. Two words are neighbours exactly when they **share a pattern**. Group the words by pattern in a dictionary (`bucket["*ot"] = [hot, dot, lot]`); the neighbours of a word are the words in the buckets of its patterns.

Emptying a bucket after its first use (`pop`) is a small but important speed-up: all words of a bucket get their distance at that moment, so the bucket is never needed again. The total work is O(k * length^2). If `end` is not in the dictionary, the answer is 0.

statement: A word ladder from `begin` to `end` is a sequence of words that starts with `begin`, ends with `end`, and in which every two neighbouring words differ in exactly one letter and every word except `begin` is in the dictionary. Print the number of words of the shortest ladder (including `begin` and `end`), or 0 if there is none.
inputFormat: The first line has `begin` and `end`: two words of the same length.
The second line has `k`, the number of words in the dictionary.
The third line has the `k` words of the dictionary (all of the same length as `begin`).
outputFormat: Print the number of words or 0.
constraints: All words have the same length, from 1 to 10 lowercase letters.

examples.input:
hit cog
6
hot dot dog lot log cog
examples.note: hit, hot, dot, dog, cog: 5 words.

hints: Replace each letter in turn by * to get the patterns of a word.
Words that share a pattern are neighbours: keep a dictionary from a pattern to the list of its words.
Run a breadth-first search from begin, counting words; print 0 if end is never reached.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

begin, end = input().split()
k = int(input())
words = input().split()

explanation: Words are grouped by their patterns with one wildcard letter; the neighbours of a word are the words in its buckets, each bucket is used once. A breadth-first search from begin counts the words of the shortest ladder, 0 if end is not reached or not in the dictionary.
solution.complexity: Time O(k * length^2), space O(k * length^2).
